findings.title: Statusline budget always null post-migration
findings.problem: resolveBudget() destructures codeMieUrl and userEmail directly from the raw profile object (config.profiles[config.activeProfile]) read straight from the JSON config file, but migration 006 moves codeMieUrl out of the profile into the new top-level workspace object.
findings.impact: After migration 006 runs, codeMieUrl is always undefined on the raw profile, so the `!codeMieUrl` guard on line 216 is always true and resolveBudget() silently returns { budget: null, budgetError: null } for every SSO user — the statusline's budget segment permanently disappears with no error surfaced, and this file is not part of the diff so nothing flags the break.
findings.recommendation: Update statusline.mjs to read codeMieUrl from config.workspace (and reconcile userEmail with the top-level MultiProviderConfig.userEmail) instead of the per-profile object, mirroring the new WorkspaceConfig split.

findings.title: Stale ProviderProfile literal breaks typecheck
findings.problem: The pre-existing test 'should accept profile with SSO fields' constructs a ProviderProfile object literal with codeMieUrl and codeMieIntegration, both of which this diff removes from the ProviderProfile interface (moved to WorkspaceConfig).
findings.impact: npm run typecheck/ci fails to compile this file, blocking the build/CI pipeline for this change.
findings.recommendation: Update the test literal to drop codeMieUrl/codeMieIntegration from the ProviderProfile object (or assert them separately against a WorkspaceConfig/CodeMieConfigOptions value) so it matches the new interface shape.

findings.title: Migration writes empty workspace, breaks fallback
findings.problem: migrate() always returns { ...config, profiles, workspace } (lines 92-96), even when no profile ever defined a WORKSPACE_KEYS field, so workspace ends up {} for every project that has a local .codemie/ config. resolveWorkspace() (src/utils/config.ts:211) treats any defined workspace — including {} — as a whole-object override and never falls back to the global scope.
findings.impact: On next CLI invocation, every existing project with a local config permanently loses inherited global codeMieUrl/hooks/metrics/plugins/skillsSearchUrl/claudeAutocompactPct, even if that project's profiles never touched a workspace-moving field. Both initProjectConfig (line 904) and saveProfile (line 605) correctly guard with Object.keys(...).length > 0 before writing workspace; the migration is the only write path missing that guard, and no test exercises the migrated-then-resolved path together.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the same non-empty guard in migrate() — only include workspace in the returned config when Object.keys(workspace).length > 0 — or make resolveWorkspace() fall back to global when the local workspace is empty.

findings.title: applyProjectOnly contradicts its removal AC
findings.problem: The spec/AC explicitly requires PROJECT_FIELDS, filterProjectFields, shouldPreserveProjectContext, and applyProjectOnly to be removed from src/utils/config.ts. The first three are gone, but applyProjectOnly still exists as a local const in both load() (line 124) and loadWithSources() (line 1219), still gating whether the local team profile's provider/model/credentials apply when a different global profile is selected.
findings.impact: The acceptance criterion is marked partial: literally unmet, even though the variable appears to still serve a legitimate purpose (preventing a mismatched local profile's credentials from leaking onto a different active global profile). It is unclear whether the AC's wording was meant literally (eliminate the symbol and find another way to prevent credential leakage) or whether the AC should be revised to reflect applyProjectOnly as an intentional carry-over under the new design.
findings.recommendation: Get product/spec-owner sign-off on whether applyProjectOnly should be removed (and replaced with an equivalent mechanism) or whether the AC text should be revised to reflect it as an intentional retained gate.

findings.title: workspace: null crashes ConfigLoader.load()
findings.problem: resolveWorkspace() only checks localMultiConfig.workspace !== undefined before returning it; a hand-edited or externally-written config with "workspace": null passes that check (null !== undefined) and is returned as-is.
findings.impact: load() then calls removeUndefined(workspace) (line 136), which does Object.entries(obj) — Object.entries(null) throws a TypeError, crashing every ConfigLoader.load()/loadWithSources() call for that project until the file is manually fixed.
findings.recommendation: Guard both the resolveWorkspace() return check and removeUndefined() against null, e.g. `workspace != null` (loose) or an explicit null check before Object.entries.

findings.title: loadWithSources mislabels workspace source
findings.problem: The workspace ConfigLayer pushed into loadWithSources() is hardcoded to source: 'project' (line 1246), independent of whether resolveWorkspace() actually resolved the value from the local scope or fell back to the global scope.
findings.impact: codemie profile status --show-sources reports codeMieUrl/codeMieProject/hooks/etc. as (project)-sourced even when only the global ~/.codemie config supplied them, misleading users debugging which scope owns a value. The one test exercising this path ('loadWithSources reports workspace-resolved codeMieUrl with source project' in config-project-override.test.ts) sets up a global-only scenario and locks in the wrong label as expected, so the bug is pinned rather than caught.
findings.recommendation: Set the workspace layer's source conditionally, e.g. localMultiConfig.workspace !== undefined ? 'project' : 'global', and fix the test to assert 'global' for the global-only scenario.

Decision recorded in code-review-fix-evidence.json: applyProjectOnly is retained by design (still gates provider-identity resolution to prevent credential leakage across profiles), not removed. spec.md:44 was revised accordingly and the revision matches the unchanged code at src/utils/config.ts:124 and :1224 — code and spec are now consistent, resolving the ambiguity without a code change

'project' : 'global' and uses it as the ConfigLayer's source instead of the hardcoded 'project'; config-project-override.test.ts:679-735 replaces the previously-pinned wrong assertion with two tests, one per scope ('reports a global-only workspace value with source "global"' and 'reports a local-scope workspace value with source "project"')
